newsitem.title: INDIA: Sikh-Hindu alliance gets landslide win in Punjab.
newsitem.headline: Sikh-Hindu alliance gets landslide win in Punjab.

text.p: A Sikh-Hindu alliance led by the pro-Sikh Akali Dal party won a landslide victory in India's northern state of Punjab on Monday, taking 92 of the 117 seats in the local assembly, officials said.
They said the Akali Dal party had won 74 seats in Friday's polls, and its Hindu nationalist ally, India's main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), had won 18 seats, with all seats declared.

Election officials said the Congress party, which ruled the agriculturally-rich state for five years since the previous election, was routed, and won only 14 seats. This compared with 87 in 1992, when local polls marked the end of a Sikh separatist war.
The Communist Party of India won two seats, while the low-caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and a pro-separatist Akali Dal faction won one seat each. Independents won seven.
The pro-separatist faction of the Akali Dal had fielded candidates in 29 constituencies, but won in only one.
The 1992 elections marked the containment of a decade-long Sikh separatist rebellion in the state, but voting was then held in an atmosphere of fear and the threat of violence.
